Entries.Text: The player's equipment (armor, weapons and their cloth, in the parts folder) keeps its size.
Projectiles (bullet size, speed and range), knockback distances, the AI's sight, hearing and leash ranges, distances written in its Lua scripts, and effects keep their size.
Scale
Make a scaled copy under a new character ID (the original stays as it is), or scale the character itself.

Time Act Distances ({0} files)

Distances in the character's time act events: how far its attacks lunge to reach the target (BoostRootMotionToReachTarget) and, in Elden Ring and Nightreign, its ground offsets. Found by their names in the game's time act template.
Attack Hit Radii ({0} attacks, {1} to copy)

The hit sphere radii of the character's attacks (AtkParam_Npc, through its BehaviorParam rows). Attacks other characters also use are copied to new rows and this character pointed at the copies, so the others keep theirs ({0} behavior variations copied whole, as other models use them).
Lock-On Camera ({0} rows, {1} to copy)
How far the camera sits and how high it aims when the player locks on to this character (LockCamParam camera distance and pivot height). A row other characters share is copied for this one.
AI Spacing ({0} rows)
The near, mid, far and out distances the AI fights at, and its arrive distances (NpcThinkParam; only Bloodborne keeps these in params).

Scale
How much bigger the character becomes: 2 is twice the size, 0.5 half.
The factor every length is multiplied by. It is used when you press Scale.
Use a scale between 0.05 and 20.
Parts
Which parts of the character are scaled. Leave all three ticked unless you know you want only some.
Models ({0})
Every model in the chrbnd: vertices, bones, dummy polys and bounding boxes.
Skeleton
The animation skeleton's rest pose in the anibnd.
Animation Clips ({0})
Every clip's bone movement and root motion, so the character walks the right distance for its size. Turns are kept exactly.
Ragdoll ({0} physics files)
The chrbnd's physics file: the ragdoll's bodies, shapes, joints and mass (in Armored Core VI also the second physics file), so the character falls and collides as its new size when it dies.
Scale mass with size
On: the ragdoll's mass grows with its volume (scale cubed), so a bigger character is much heavier and harder to push. Off: it keeps its mass, spread over the bigger body.
Cloth ({0} files)
The chrbnd's cloth: its rest shape, link lengths, collision shapes and how the cloth follows the body. Cloth keeps its mass and stiffness, so it hangs and swings as before at the new size.
Behavior ({0} files)
The behavior character file: foot and hand IK (how far the feet reach for the ground) and, in DS3 and Bloodborne, the character controller capsule.
Body Size Params ({0} NpcParam rows)

The capsule the character collides with the map and other characters with (height, radius, offset) and other body size fields, on every NpcParam row that uses this model. Edited in the Param Editor as one undo step; save the params to keep them.
The project's params aren't loaded (or have no NpcParam), so the body size fields can't be edited.
